text:
Alex C: heads-up — ap-east1 control plane is spiking 500s after the GPU pool scaleout at ~03:12 UTC. controller-manager leader flips observed.
infra-bot: ALERT: apiserver_latency_high ap-east1 (p90 1.8s -> 6.2s) · 03:14 UTC · incident: auto-opened
Priya S: oncall here, looking. did scaleout attach new NVMe-backed nodes around that time?
Alex C: yes, autoscaler kicked and added 10 on-demand GPU nodes to the p4-pool between 03:10–03:13.
Jon R: seeing high iowait on control plane host that runs etcd snapshots - NVMe queue depth > 200. likely snapshot + attach churn.
Marta L: also noticed packet retransmits from the new SR-IOV NICs on those nodes, looks like MTU mismatch (frag) between host and fabric
Priya S: can you paste the etcd log / brief iostat? quick grep helps.
Jon R: iostat -x 1 3 output:
```
Device      r/s   w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s %rrqm %wrqm r_await w_await aqu-sz
nvme0n1    45.2  980.1  1024  250000   0.00  15.00  0.0   1.5   3.2    12.6   5.1
```
Jon R: /var/log/etcd/etcd.log snippet:
```
2026-03-20T03:12:31 etcdserver: snapshot saved to file/db/snap-... size=1.2G dur=4.3s iowait=0.78
2026-03-20T03:12:33 transport: write tcp 10.3.2.5:2379: write: connection reset by peer
2026-03-20T03:12:34 leader transfer requested
```
Marta L: SR-IOV VF MTU was left at 1500 on the new GPU hosts while fabric expects 9000 — fragmentation causing retransmits + higher CPU on networking stack
Priya S: so combined issue: massive snapshot IO + fragmented packets -> etcd RPC failures -> apiserver retries -> request pileup -> controller-manager elections. makes sense.
Alex C: immediate mitigation ideas?
Jon R: 1) pause the scheduled full snapshot job for 30m (backup pipeline) 2) set etcd compaction retention to 1h temporarily `ETCD_AUTO_COMPACTION_RETENTION=1` 3) move snapshot writes to separate NVMe if possible or lower write concurrency
Marta L: 4) roll a quick config change on the new GPU host AMI to set VF MTU=9000 and reattach (or hotfix with `ip link set dev ethvf mtu 9000`), but reattach may cause pod disruption.
Priya S: we should also cap autoscaler burst to avoid adding so many nodes at once — can reduce `max_unready_percentage` and set `scaleUpLimit` to 4 for p4-pool.
Alex C: agree. cost note: that burst added ~10 P4s for ~15 min — estimate ~$2.8k surge this hour. we need budget guardrails for dedicated vs on-demand.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment to gpu-pool image v2.3.1 started at 03:16 UTC · canary 2/10 nodes
Jon R: temp control-plane knob: increase kube-apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` from 250 -> 400 to make bursts less likely to be refused (short-term), but it's a band-aid.
Priya S: action items: Jon pause snapshots + tweak compaction (doing now), Marta push MTU hotfix to 3/10 new nodes then schedule full rollout if stable, Alex update autoscaler limits and cost playbook, I'll coordinate rollback if anything degrades.
Marta L: running hotfix on one node: `ip link set dev ethvf0 mtu 9000 && ethtool -S ethvf0 | grep tx_errors` -> checking
Alex C: ack. leave backup paused for 30m and then re-evaluate.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-198 created · severity: P2 · assignees: Priya S, Jon R · 03:18 UTC
Priya S: marking soothing alert · will post follow-up summary once we stabilize :thumbsup:
Alex C: summary for postmortem: autoscaler burst + NVMe snapshot IO + SR-IOV MTU mismatch -> etcd RPC failures -> apiserver latency -> controller-manager leader flips -> workload thrash + cost spike. mitigation: autoscaler caps, snapshot throttling, MTU fix, move snapshots off critical NVMe. assign PM to add cost guardrails.
Jon R: I'll open a short runbook PR with the snapshot throttling steps + exact commands.
Marta L: will verify NIC firmware + add automated MTU check to node bootstrap.
Priya S: thanks all, keeping oncall loop open until 04:00 UTC for rollback window.
Alex C: :raised_hands: good work — let's keep chat for updates only.
